bindings_patch_style_constraints: Prefer not to add PHY-driver C headers to `bindings_helper.h` unless the abstraction plan proves they are still needed after wrapper design.
Do not mirror legacy C include lists into Rust bindings when the Rust driver can stay within `kernel::net::phy` and `kernel::uapi`.

messages.all_implemented: The tree already exposes the required PHY abstraction surfaces ({implemented_areas}); the current module can stay inside the existing PHY layer.
messages.baseline_only: The tree already has a Rust PHY baseline, but `{module_id}` still needs explicit planning for the remaining module-specific PHY surfaces.
messages.partial: The tree exposes partial PHY support; `{module_id}` still needs the remaining planned PHY surfaces after {implemented_areas_or_default}.

driver_generation_rules: Driver code may borrow style from existing Rust PHY drivers, but must stay within the safe `kernel::net::phy` driver surface.
Do not read or write PHY registers through raw `bindings::*`; keep all access through `phy::Device` and typed register wrappers.
Any new PHY callback beyond the current artifact boundary requires updating the profile and artifacts first.

driver_side_rules: Do not use `unsafe` in driver code, including `unsafe impl`, `unsafe fn`, or `unsafe {}` blocks.
Do not reference `bindings::*` directly from driver code; keep all PHYLIB interaction inside `kernel::net::phy`.
Do not add raw pointer manipulation or direct MDIO register FFI calls in `{driver_rust_path}`.
Keep driver logic restricted to the callback set declared in `translation-plan.json`.
